Indore to Halifax to Toronto

I've never really stayed in one lane, and honestly I think that's helped me. Every new city meant a new system to learn and new people to get to know.

I grew up in Indore, India, a city that runs on good food and warm people. I studied commerce and computer applications there, then packed up in 2024 and moved to Halifax for my Master of Digital Innovation at Dalhousie.

Since then I've worked in classrooms, prospected for a tech company, helped customers at Lindt, done research at Dalhousie and joined the support team for a huge hospital system go-live. It sounds like a lot of different things, but it's really one thing: I like being the person people can count on. Somewhere along the way, my friends also named my tiramisu after me.

Writing sample

A short help article, written the way I write job aids for staff: simple words, one step at a time, and why it matters.

Help centre · 3 min read

Get your support ticket solved faster

For anyone reporting a problem with a new system. Written from the other side of 700+ support calls.

Help articleFor everyday users

Before you call or send a ticket

Most delays happen because support has to come back and ask you more questions. Have these five things ready and there's a good chance we can fix it on the first try.

  1. Tell us what you were trying to do. "Place a lab order for a patient" helps us much more than "the system isn't working."
  2. Tell us exactly what happened. Copy the error message word for word, or take a screenshot. Hide any patient or customer details first.
  3. Try it once more. Does it happen every time, or only sometimes? Just for you, or for your coworkers too?
  4. Tell us where and when. Your unit or department, which computer you used, and roughly what time it happened.
  5. Tell us how urgent it is. Is someone stuck and unable to work, or is there a way around it for now?

What a great ticket looks like

Trying to: print a discharge summary What happened: "Unable to print: no default printer" (screenshot attached) Happens: every time, 2 coworkers see it too Where / when: 3rd floor unit, workstation 12, since 9:40 am Urgency: holding up discharges, no workaround yet

Why this helps: we can see the problem for ourselves, send it to the right team the first time, and skip all the back-and-forth.
